newsitem.title: PERU: Japan envoy saw Peru breaking point before crisis.
newsitem.headline: Japan envoy saw Peru breaking point before crisis.

text.p: Japanese Ambassador Morihisa Aoki, in a Christmas greeting sent to friends just before he and more than 500 of his guests were taken hostage at a reception at his home, said Peru's tense social situation had reached breaking point.

"The patience of the grassroots citizens (of Peru) who have waited in hope for Fujimori to turn the economy around has come to a breaking point," he wrote, referring to President Alberto Fujimori, whose parents came to Peru from Japan.

"The fact that his popularity rate, which was at 76 percent in January last year, fell to 48 percent in October clearly indicates this mood," he said in the Christmas and New Year greeting card released on Tuesday by Japanese officials. The officials did not say exactly when the letter, signed by Aoki and his wife Naoko, was written.

Aoki and about 140 hostages were being held captive in the ambassador's residence for a seventh day on Tuesday after Marxist guerrillas stormed a party Aoki held to celebrate Japanese Emperor Akihito's birthday. The Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels demanded the release of more than 400 jailed comrades, as well as economic reforms -- demands rejected by Fujimori.

"The last year was a year of trials for the Fujimori government. The economy faltered, and while poverty and unemployment, the biggest issues in this country, showed no signs of improvement, there was political disharmony within the administration," Aoki wrote.

"It could be said that the Fujimori government has come to a critical juncture," he said, adding: "The president himself realises this situation. But he is full of spirit, and I heard him telling a Japanese visitor that this is the reason he loves his job."
Aoki has won resounding praise from hostages already freed as a "hero" who stood up to the rebels to protect his guests.
